title: AI Engineer
description:
About Bizmoni Corp.
Bizmoni is building an AI Business Network designed to help people and businesses connect, earn, learn, and grow in the AI era.
As a seed-stage, pre-revenue company, we are strengthening our platform, growing our global ecosystem, and laying the foundations for future funding and scale. This is an opportunity to join an entrepreneurial, international team and help shape both the product and the business.
About the Role
Architecture and platform build

• Design and build our LLM infrastructure from scratch: model serving, orchestration, data pipelines, vector storage and observability.

• Make and document key build-vs-buy decisions, including hosted APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) versus self-hosted open-weight models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen).

• Stand up scalable, cost-efficient inference using tools such as vLLM, TGI or Triton, on GPU and CPU infrastructure.

• Build the cloud foundations on [AWS / Azure / GCP] using infrastructure-as-code (Terraform or similar), Docker and Kubernetes.

LLM application engineering

• Build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines: ingestion, chunking, embeddings, hybrid search and re-ranking.

• Develop agentic workflows, tool use and function calling for production use cases.

• Fine-tune and adapt models where it adds value (LoRA/QLoRA, PEFT), and know when prompting or retrieval is the better answer.

• Expose AI capabilities through well-designed Python APIs (FastAPI or similar) for product and engineering teams.

Quality, reliability and safety

• Build evaluation frameworks to measure accuracy, hallucination, latency and cost, and use them to gate releases.

• Implement monitoring, tracing and alerting for LLM services (e.g. LangSmith, Langfuse, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus/Grafana).

• Put guardrails in place for data privacy, prompt injection, PII handling and GDPR compliance.

• Own CI/CD and MLOps practices for models, prompts and pipelines.

Leadership and collaboration

• Set coding standards, write clear technical documentation and review code.

• Partner with product, data and engineering leads to turn business problems into shipped AI features.

• Help shape future AI hiring and mentor engineers as the team grows.

What you'll bring

•
Expert, hands-on Python. 5+ years writing production Python daily: async, typing, packaging, testing (pytest) and performance profiling. You write the code, not just the design doc.

•
Built LLM systems in production. At least 2 years shipping LLM-powered products to real users, including at least one platform or major system you built from scratch.

•
Infrastructure depth. Strong experience with Docker, Kubernetes and at least one major cloud (AWS, Azure or GCP), plus infrastructure-as-code.

•
Model serving and optimisation. Practical knowledge of inference servers, GPU utilisation, batching, quantisation and caching to manage latency and cost.

•
RAG and data. Hands-on with embeddings and vector databases (pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant or similar) and building reliable data pipelines.

•
ML fundamentals. Solid understanding of transformers, tokenisation and fine-tuning, with experience using PyTorch and Hugging Face.

•
Engineering discipline. CI/CD, observability, API design and writing software others can maintain.

•
Ownership. Comfortable making architectural calls with incomplete information, explaining trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders, and working without a ready-made playbook.

Nice to have

• Experience as the first or founding AI/ML engineer at a start-up or scale-up.

• Agent frameworks and protocols such as LangGraph, LlamaIndex, DSPy or Model Context Protocol (MCP).

• Distributed training or multi-GPU work (DeepSpeed, FSDP, Ray).

• Working in a regulated sector (fintech, healthcare, public sector) and familiarity with the EU AI Act.

• Some Rust, Go or TypeScript alongside Python.

• Open-source contributions, published projects or technical writing in the LLM space.

title: German Speaking Go Coding Evaluation Specialist
description:
Join a short, paid project that tests whether AI coding agents work as well on instructions written in the target language as they do in English. Your language skills and technical background decide where you fit.
About the project
Welo Data is helping evaluate how well AI coding agents perform when the instructions they receive are written in languages other than English. Agents are given a real software engineering task in a code repository, and automated tests check whether they solved it. The code, repositories and tests stay exactly as they are. Only the human-written instructions change language, so the quality of every instruction directly affects the result.
About the roles
There are two roles on this project. We place you in one of them based on your experience & skillsets.

• Translator: translate English software engineering task briefs into the target language. You keep every requirement, constraint and success condition, and you leave commands, file paths, API names, code and test conditions exactly as written in English. This role suits people with a stronger technical background, and translation experience is a plus.

• Reviewer: compare each translation with the English source, check that nothing is missing, added or changed in meaning, correct errors, and log each correction by error type. This role suits people with strong translation, editing or review experience and enough technical familiarity to read code context.

Who we are looking for

• Native or near-native writing in the target language, and strong reading ability in English.

• Either professional experience in translation, editing, review or technical writing, or a software background combined with excellent writing in the target language

• Comfort reading technical text. Coding experience is a strong plus for the translation role and helpful for the review role.

• Close attention to detail. In this project, a dropped clause can make a task fail.

Project at a glance

• Project duration: one week since the mid of November

• Language: German

• Project time commitment: 6 hours per person

• Project compensation: US$72.5 - US$87.5 per hour

• Work location: fully remote in Germany

How selection works (major steps)

• Screening questions: about 2 minutes. They cover your language background, translation and review experience, which programming languages you know and how well, and your availability.

• Language test: short exercises in the target language.

• Programming skills assessment: you will be invited to another opportunity, in the programming language you know best (Rust, Go, Python, or TypeScript / JavaScript). It confirms your technical level and places you in a language track.

• Financial Onboarding & Role placement: complete the financial onboarding with Welo Data. In the meanwhile, you will be informed about the decision whether you are placed in the initial translation role or the review role.

• Production: once you finish all steps above, our project team will contact you for production.

The Role
Crimson is replacing Salesforce with Salesflow, an AI-native CRM we build in-house. It runs the whole sales journey: lead intake, meeting scheduling, call transcription analysis, AI-drafted appraisals, contracts and e-signature, and invoicing. It is live for our US sales team today and rolls out to every other market over the coming months.
Our team is small and builder-heavy, and the rate of growth has made it hard to keep the underlying infrastructure and logic clean and tidy. As examples, CI checks things that have been fully deprecated, newly added modules do not always take into account legacy compatibility, and bug fixes are sometimes too narrow in scope, fixing the place the problem was seen and not the underlying cause. Compounding the above is that the code itself is for the most part written by AI - this is what enabled us to build a fully working CRM in a matter of months, but is what makes it very easy to inadvertently cross wires during development.
We are looking for the person who fixes this: you will own the backend view of the system as a whole and maintain the code that glues everything together. title: Learner Outcomes Research Intern
description:
At peopleworth , we support work where people and performance thrive. As part of our Employer Group, we work with a variety of forward-thinking partners and are excited to share this opportunity that sits within our growing group.
Role Overview
This is a fixed-term internship opportunity focused on researching and updating career outcome information for past learners. The role will involve reviewing approximately 1,500 learner records from 2024 and 2025, using publicly available professional information and internal records to identify new roles, promotions, or other relevant career outcomes.
The initial contract is expected to run for approximately 8 weeks, working 3 days per week, with an estimated total commitment of around 180 hours. There may be an opportunity to extend the internship to approximately 12 weeks to support additional cohorts and help document a repeatable process for future use.
This role is well suited to someone who is organised, detail-oriented, comfortable working with spreadsheets and online research tools, and able to follow a clear process when handling personal information.
Requirements

• Strong attention to detail and the ability to work accurately across a high volume of records.

• Confidence conducting structured online research and comparing information across different sources.

• Working knowledge of LinkedIn and the ability to navigate professional profiles effectively for research purposes.

• Practical experience using Google Sheets, including entering, organising, reviewing, and updating information accurately.

• Comfort using Gmail and Google Docs in a professional or academic environment.

• Working knowledge of Microsoft Word or similar document-processing software.

• Ability to follow a written process consistently while recognising when information is unclear and needs to be escalated.

• Strong organisational and time-management skills with the ability to work independently across a defined workload.

• Good written communication skills and confidence working with structured data and administrative information.

• A responsible approach to confidentiality, personal information, and data protection.

• Access to a reliable laptop or computer suitable for completing online research and administrative work.

• Access to a stable internet connection for the duration of the internship.

• Previous administrative, research, data-capture, recruitment, education, customer-support, or similar experience would be advantageous but is not essential.

Key Responsibilities

• Review past learner records and identify where career outcome information is currently missing.

• Research publicly available LinkedIn information to identify whether learners have moved into a new role, received a promotion, or experienced another relevant career outcome since completing their programme.

• Record verified career outcomes accurately and consistently in the designated outcomes tracking sheet.

• Log responses received from follow-up emails sent to learners whose outcomes cannot be confirmed through available information.

• Follow a documented research and verification process to ensure consistent and reliable data capture.

• Refer uncertain or ambiguous matches to the designated reviewer or coach before recording an outcome.

• Maintain accurate records of research completed, outcomes identified, and cases requiring further review.

• Handle learner personal information carefully and in accordance with confidentiality, privacy, and data-protection requirements.

• Use Gmail, Google Sheets, Google Docs, Microsoft Word, LinkedIn, and related tools to complete research, record information, and support project administration.

• Support the documentation and improvement of the research process so that the approach can be repeated for future learner cohorts.

Benefits
Collaborative, people-centred performance culture.
Opportunities to grow in a fast-paced environment.
